provenance.publisher: Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN), part of the Virginia Department of Emergency Management

known_limitations: Cartographic/analysis use only per the publisher's own disclaimer; not a legal description or a property survey. Boundary questions with legal consequence go to the locality, not this layer.

Geometry is returned simplified (server-side generalization) so a polygon fits an inline response; the unsimplified boundary is not exposed until the result-resource store exists. Simplified vertices can sit tens of metres off the true line — never use them to decide which side of a boundary a specific address falls on.

Layer publishes no layer-level last-edit date (editingInfo is absent on both layers), so envelope source_updated_at is null. The per-record LASTUPDATE field IS mapped and surfaced per boundary, so each returned record carries its own vintage even though the layer does not.

The localities layer carries 134 rows for Virginia's 133 counties and independent cities. Prince George County (FIPS 51149) is published as two separate polygons sharing one FIPS and GNIS, a 281 sq mi body and a 0.0076 sq mi sliver. Both are returned; neither is silently dropped. See ../../design/source-quirks.md.
Towns layer covers incorporated towns only. Virginia's unincorporated communities and CDPs have no polygon here, and absence is not evidence that a place does not exist.

calls.note: Code of Virginia section text with its own citation history

results.heading: § 1-500. The great seal.
paragraphs: The great seal of the Commonwealth shall consist of two metallic discs, two and one-fourth inches in diameter, with an ornamental border one fourth of an inch wide, with such words and figures engraved as follows: On the obverse, Virtus, the genius of the Commonwealth, dressed as an Amazon, resting on a spear in her right hand, point downward, touching the earth; and holding in her left hand, a sheathed sword, or parazonium, pointing upward; her head erect and face upturned; her left foot on the form of Tyranny represented by the prostrate body of a man, with his head to her left, his fallen crown nearby, a broken chain in his left hand, and a scourge in his right. Above the group and within the border conforming therewith, shall be the word "Virginia," and, in the space below, on a curved line, shall be the motto, "Sic Semper Tyrannis." On the reverse, shall be placed a group consisting of Libertas, holding a wand and pileus in her right hand; on her right, Aeternitas, with a globe and phoenix in her right hand; on the left of Libertas, Ceres, with a cornucopia in her left hand, and an ear of wheat in her right; over this device, in a curved line, the word "Perseverando."
